subject: db
title: Relational algebra
description: Translate a question in plain language into an algebra expression.
promptTemplate: Give a schema with 2–3 relations and a question. easy: selection and projection. medium: join and renaming. exam: difference or division. Notation: σ, π, ⋈, ρ, ∪, −, ÷ (ASCII stand-ins sigma, pi, join, rho, union, minus, div are fine). When checking: operator by operator from the inside out, checking attribute names and the schemas of intermediate results.

drills.prompt: Which operator picks **rows** that satisfy a condition?
Which operators can change the **number of columns**?
drills.explanation: Projection keeps some columns, a join combines the columns of both relations. Selection and union keep the schema.

drills.prompt: R has 3 rows and S has 4 rows. How many rows does R × S have?
drills.explanation: The cross product pairs every row of R with every row of S: 3 · 4.

drills.prompt: Which operator answers questions like "students who attended **all** lectures"? Give its name.
drills.explanation: Division R ÷ S returns the values that appear in R together with every tuple of S.

drills.prompt:
Schema: `Student(sid, name)`, `Enrolled(sid, cid)`.

Write an expression for the **names** of all students enrolled in course `'db'`.
drills.solution:
`π_name(σ_cid='db'(Enrolled) ⋈ Student)`

Select first, so the join works on fewer rows; project on name at the end.
